edges.description: Other signaling pathways drive proliferation in absence of ER
Multiple activated pathways drive aggressive phenotype
DNA repair defects lead to mutation accumulation
Accumulated driver lesions and chromosomal instability fuel clonal evolution and the aggressive clinical course.
Suppression of M1 polarization promotes tumor progression.
Macrophages are a principal source of the CD8-recruiting chemokine CXCL9, so an immunosuppressed macrophage compartment leaves the tumor short of it.
Too little CXCL9 in the tumor means too little CXCR3-driven chemotaxis of CD8-positive T cells across the tumor margin.
Without cytotoxic T cells in the tumor, immune control of outgrowth is lost.

nodes.description: TNBC is characterized by high proliferation rates, early metastasis (especially to viscera and brain), and shorter time to recurrence compared to other breast cancer subtypes. The aggressive biology reflects activation of multiple oncogenic pathways and loss of tumor suppressors.

evidence.reference_title: Triple negative breast cancer: Pitfalls and progress.
evidence.snippet: It accounts for 10-15% of incident breast cancers and carries the worst prognosis.

nodes.description: In the absence of hormone receptor signaling, TNBC is driven by alternative oncogenic pathways including EGFR signaling, PI3K-AKT-mTOR activation, and Wnt/beta-catenin signaling. Many TNBCs have TP53 mutations eliminating this tumor suppressor checkpoint.

biological_processes: epidermal growth factor receptor signaling pathway

nodes.description: TNBC tumors are poorly infiltrated by CD8-positive cytotoxic T lymphocytes, which is the proximate reason immune checkpoint blockade benefits only a minority of patients: a drug that releases a brake on T cells does little where the T cells are not present. Supplying CXCL9 reverses the exclusion in model systems.

biological_processes: T cell chemotaxis into the tumor

evidence.reference_title: Co-delivery of chemokine CXCL9 and costimulatory ligand TNFSF9 by mesenchymal stem cells reprograms the immune microenvironment for triple-negative breast cancer.
evidence.snippet: Due to limited tumor immune infiltration in TNBC, the effectiveness of immunotherapy is constrained

evidence.reference_title: Targeting tumor-associated macrophages using mRNA lipid nanoparticles for cytotoxic T lymphocyte-mediated cancer immunotherapy.
evidence.snippet: codelivery of a Toll-like receptor agonist and CXCL9-encoding mRNA encapsulated in our Ab-LNP successfully ameliorates immunosuppression and improves tumor infiltration and activity of CTLs

nodes.description: A significant subset of TNBC (~20%) harbors germline or somatic BRCA1/2 mutations resulting in homologous recombination deficiency. This creates sensitivity to platinum chemotherapy and PARP inhibitors through synthetic lethality.

evidence.reference_title: PARP Inhibitors in Triple-Negative Breast Cancer Including Those With BRCA Mutations.
evidence.snippet: PARP inhibition causes synthetic lethality in breast cancers associated with germline BRCA1 and BRCA2 mutations and is routinely used in clinical practice for metastatic breast cancer.

nodes.description: Loss of high-fidelity double-strand-break repair, compounded by near-universal TP53 inactivation, produces a mutator phenotype and pervasive chromosomal instability. This is the enabling characteristic that supplies the driver lesions feeding the alternative oncogenic pathways and aggressive behavior of TNBC.

evidence.reference_title: Association of p53 expression with poor prognosis in patients with triple-negative breast invasive ductal carcinoma.
evidence.snippet: TP53 gene is mutated in approximately 80% of triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC).

nodes.description: CXCL9 is the dominant CXCR3 ligand recruiting cytotoxic T lymphocytes into solid tumors, and tumor-associated macrophages are a principal source of it. Where the macrophage compartment is immunosuppressed, intratumoral CXCL9 is low, and in breast cancer its expression tracks with both immune infiltration and survival. Restoring it is sufficient to pull CTLs back into the tumor, which is what makes the deficiency causal rather than merely correlated.

evidence.reference_title: Co-delivery of chemokine CXCL9 and costimulatory ligand TNFSF9 by mesenchymal stem cells reprograms the immune microenvironment for triple-negative breast cancer.
evidence.snippet: analysis of human datasets (TCGA-BRCA and Kim cohorts) revealed that tumor necrosis factor superfamily member 9 (TNFSF9) and C-X-C motif chemokine ligand (CXCL9) expressions correlate with improved prognosis and enhanced immune cell infiltration

evidence.reference_title: Targeting tumor-associated macrophages using mRNA lipid nanoparticles for cytotoxic T lymphocyte-mediated cancer immunotherapy.
evidence.snippet: targets the protein triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells 2 (TREM2) expressed by tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs)

nodes.description: TNBC lacks expression of estrogen receptor alpha (ESR1) and progesterone receptor (PGR), eliminating the growth-promoting effects of estrogen signaling that drive most breast cancers. This absence removes a key therapeutic target but also indicates fundamentally different tumor biology.

evidence.reference_title: Triple negative breast cancer: Pitfalls and progress.
evidence.snippet: Triple negative breast cancer (TNBC) is characterized by the lack of estrogen and progesterone receptor expression and lacks HER2 overexpression or gene amplification.

nodes.description: The TNBC microenvironment is immunosuppressive, with pro-inflammatory M1 macrophage polarization suppressed. Apolipoprotein C-II (APOC2) is upregulated in TNBC tissue and inversely correlates with M1 macrophage infiltration; overexpressing it in tumor cells suppresses M1 polarization and promotes tumor growth, so the effect on macrophages is tumor-cell-extrinsic. KLHL1 (a Cullin3-RING E3 ubiquitin ligase substrate adaptor) degrades APOC2 via the ubiquitin-proteasome pathway and reverses this immunosuppressive phenotype by restoring M1 polarization.

evidence.snippet: APOC2 was upregulated in TNBC tissues and was negatively correlated with M1 macrophage infiltration.
KLHL1 promoted APOC2 protein degradation through the ubiquitin-proteasome pathway, thereby enhancing M1 macrophage polarization and suppressing the malignant behavior of tumor cells.

in vivo xenograft experiments demonstrated that APOC2 reduced M1 macrophage polarization and increased tumor weight and volume, whereas KLHL1 overexpression counteracted the oncogenic effects of APOC2
